adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the test fails because EmbedController#best enqueues :retrieve_topic instead of constructing TopicRetriever. Looking at the diff, embed_controller.rb line 14 shows `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` which is correct. However, the test in embed_controller_spec.rb lines 41-45 mocks TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever) and retriever.expects(:retrieve). The test also mocks TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil). The actual controller code calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), not TopicRetriever.new directly. So the test IS incorrectly mocking - it expects TopicRetriever.new to be called but the controller actually enqueues a job. However, looking more carefully at the test setup with stubs/expects, the test would actually pass because TopicRetriever.expects(:new) would not fail if never called when using expects - it would only fail if called with wrong args. Actually, with Mocha, expects sets up an expectation that MUST be satisfied. So the finding appears correct that the test is broken.
